subject: astronomy
title: Radio and Infrared Astronomy
welcome_lead: Beyond the optical — long wavelengths reveal cold, dusty worlds.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: radio (Jodrell Bank, ALMA) and infrared (Spitzer, JWST).

concepts.def: A dish or array collecting radio waves.
Famous 76 m radio dish in the UK, operating since 1957.
Atacama Large Millimeter Array of 66 dishes in Chile.
Telescope observing thermal infrared, often cooled.
Combining signals from multiple dishes for high resolution.

walkthroughs.body_html: Radio waves pass easily through dust. Jodrell Bank's 76 m dish began work in 1957; ALMA in Chile combines 66 dishes at millimetre wavelengths for sharp imaging of cold gas and discs.
Infrared reveals cool stars, planets and dusty regions. Spitzer (2003-2020) and the JWST (launched 2021) operate in cold space to suppress their own thermal noise.
Combining signals from several dishes simulates a much larger one — interferometry. The Event Horizon Telescope used global interferometry to image M87* and Sgr A*.
